title: The Phone Bill
intro: A text from your phone company. You have just learned to doubt every text.
But some are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: Your bill is ready. View it in the My Vantel app.

screen.context: You have been with Vantel Mobile for three years.

msg.text: View it in the My Vantel app.
No action is needed if your payment is on automatic.
We will never ask you for your password or codes by text.

sender.label: Sender name
sender.why: A name alone proves nothing. What the text asks you to do is the clue.

bill.label: A monthly bill
bill.lens: You expect a bill every month.
bill.why: It matches something you expect. A surprise charge would be the warning sign.

app.label: Open the app yourself
app.lens: It sends you to the app you already have, with no link.
app.why: Pointing you to your own app is what honest companies do.

nopay.label: Nothing to pay now
nopay.lens: No payment, no fee, no deadline.
nopay.why: A real bill notice does not rush you.

reminder.label: Safety reminder
reminder.lens: It repeats that the company never asks for passwords or codes by text.
reminder.why: Real companies warn you about scams.

actions.label: Open the My Vantel app myself and look at the bill

go_ahead.line: The app showed your normal bill, paid automatically. Nothing to fear.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real notice, and your payment went through on its own.

block_report.line: That was the real Vantel Mobile. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It asked for no money, no link and no code. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asked for nothing.

golden_rule: Real company texts ask for nothing secret and point you to your own app, with no link to click.

quick_check.q: What showed this phone-company text was genuine?

options.text: It asked for nothing secret and pointed to the company's own app, with no link

quick_check.explain: Names, times and tone can all be copied. Asking for nothing, with no link, is the real sign.

hints.nudge: What is this text actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Do real companies ask for account details by text?

rows.v: Use the company's own app or a number you already know
